title: Easiest Way To Get Playtesters
author: YuukiCrypto
selftext:
Hey all!

One of the hardest parts of game development is obtaining valuable playtesters. The amount of "i emailed X number of influencers for my game" posts I have seen is incredible. Why are we still spamming creators just to play our games? I am not saying you should not, I am just questioning why there is not a better option for small, indie creators...



This always confused me, because playing games is fun and developers NEED gamers in order to make good games, so where are all the playtesters?

There are loads of places to get your game tested once it is in a finished state, and even most AAA gaming studios have full playtesting departments. Playtesting is crucial to making a good game, so why is it so hard for indie devs to CONSISTENTLY find playtesters when they need one?

No more...

Today I am releasing: [https://theplaytest.io/](https://theplaytest.io/)

**ThePlayTest** is home to my custom built marketplace I am calling **Firstplay**.

**Firstplay** is a system that connects playtesters with game developers in the quickest way possible. You can **earn money for every game you playtest.** You can get your games playtested by the **best playtesters in the world.**

  
You can submit your game here at any stage of the development process. The earlier you ask for feedback, the better. Getting play testers to tell you if your game is good or bad early will save you so much money in the long term...

The more games you test, the better rating you can receive if you're doing a good job. Before accepting any playtester, a game dev can look through your profile and reviews to get an understanding of how good of a playtester you are.

You can choose to pay $1 per test or $1000 per test. Or maybe you need a tester for one minute for $1, or 10 minutes for $1, your choice. If you don't get playtesters or get low rated testers trying to improve their rating, it is up to you. The goal is the market chooses the price. Not me.  
  
Just need one playtester, great. Need 100 UNIQUE 5-star playtesters? There is no better way to find them than [theplaytester.io](http://theplaytester.io)

Earn for playing games and providing invaluable feedback to indie game devs. Build up your profile by sharing Twitch and YouTube livestreams showcasing your reviews.

Share the site with others and watch the number of games you can test grow. Once you sign up, you can post whatever game you want to get tested. Or you can start testing games yourself. You can earn with every playtest.

Firstplay is designed to be simple and intuitive. You can hop in and find an inspiring indie game dev to help in under 5 minutes.

I would love to hear your thoughts. Are you going to submit your game? The idea is simple, review games honestly and earn for a good review. Receive star ratings based on your reviews. Receive more playtests offers. From a game dev perspective, you can choose your price and receive real advice from playtesters who specialize in the exact games you want.

I'll be posting my game for its first session of playtests this weekend. It has gone through several stages of changes thanks to player feedback so I know I will need more as development continues. Getting continuous player feedback when and how I want it will make a huge world of difference in quality of my game.

**Note**: I am always open to feedback and updates. I think this will help me keep my playtesters organized because if I will be gathering playtesters, I want to have a simple way to keep requesting their services while giving them exposure too. **That is what birth this idea.**

\> What are some other games that have used your service and had results getting play testers?

Faunara already gets tons of playtesters using my marketing methods. Your games will receive the same exposure

You will receive emails whenever a playtester has completed their review. You also get access to an admin dashboard for tracking your playtesters, playtesting spend, total time tested, poll results, and feedback.

comments.author: LifeguardCommon6036
comments.body: Does Firstplay allow an unpaid ($0) test, or does every listing require a paid bounty? For an AI-assisted closed alpha, can email confirmation and manual access selection happen before the session, or do reviewers need an immediately playable public link? Those two requirements would determine whether I could submit.

replies.author: YuukiCrypto
replies.body:
Hi, thanks for your interest! 

\> Does Firstplay allow an unpaid ($0) test, or does every listing require a paid bounty?

Yes, Firstplay supports free $0 unpaid tests, with no bounty or platform fee required. 

\> For an AI-assisted closed alpha, can email confirmation and manual access selection happen before the session, or do reviewers need an immediately playable public link? 

Choose “Closed alpha · arrange access after selection.” 

You can review applicants, select testers, and handle your email confirmation or allowlist before they begin. An immediately playable public link isn’t required. Share access privately, and the session deadline starts only when the tester confirms they can play.

AI-assisted closed alphas are welcome, of course.

replies.author: LifeguardCommon6036
replies.body: Astraya is now listed as a $0 closed-alpha test. The access-after-selection option worked for our email-confirmation setup. No requests yet, so I can’t speak to tester results. Thanks for clarifying those details.

replies.author: YuukiCrypto
replies.body: Great, you should start getting new playtesters soon. Thank you for posting a playtest!

comments.author: devtainer
comments.body: so is it controlled that playtester played an X amount of time? like 1 hour at least. Is there a way to get video from each playtester? voice commentary and other requests?

replies.author: YuukiCrypto
replies.body:
\> so is it controlled that playtester played an X amount of time? 

Nope. Although Firstplay has a Chrome Extension that does offer all of that. It is OPTIONAL. If a game developer wants to require that then they can. The extension requires the playtester to login. Once logged in on the extension, they will be able to see all of their accepted playtests.   
  
Then they can use the chrome extension to record their desktop, take screenshots, voiceover, submit notes, etc. Those notes automatically get attached to the playtest review if the playtesters approves\*

You will have full access to all of that information when they submit their final playtest review. Timers are hit or miss so requiring it seems unnecessary. I rather leave that option up to the Game Developers themselves.
